_note: Diagnosis only -- no code changed by this record. Parity bug B (task #39): why PDFium's arm produces roughly one paragraph per LINE where PyMuPDF's arrives with paragraphs already formed. Measured at da15f47 in the canonical container.
question_asked: Is the difference a units/rounding artifact in our extraction, or a real geometric difference between the parsers' lines?
answer: Neither. The line geometry is near-identical on the two arms. The difference is that PyMuPDF NEVER RUNS our block assembly -- parse.py takes blocks straight from MuPDF's structured-text analysis (parse.py:211, `TextBlock(lines=lines, bbox=tuple(blk['bbox']))`) -- while parse_pdfium must synthesise them, and the synthesis has a defect that shatters either parser's lines equally.

line_geometry_is_not_the_variable._note: y06, first 40 pages, at the IR.
line_geometry_is_not_the_variable.conclusion: PDFium's char boxes are em boxes, not tight ink boxes; the earlier mode-0-versus-mode-3 difference measured at the Para level in infer is a downstream consequence of block shattering, not a cause.

the_control._note: parse_pdfium._build_blocks run over PyMuPDF's OWN lines. First 40 pages.

x10_chrome_tables_plain._note: Our assembly over PyMuPDF's lines reproduces PDFium's numbers EXACTLY. Same rule, same answer, different input -- so the rule is the variable, not the parser.

chain: _column_split returns AT MOST ONE gutter, and under-detects: on y06 it found a gutter on 6 of 40 pages under PyMuPDF's lines and 8 of 40 under PDFium's, on a document that is two- and three-column throughout.

When the columns are not separated, the line list handed to _build_blocks_one is interleaved in reading order -- left line 1, right line 1, left line 2 -- so consecutive baseline deltas are near zero.
_body_pitch and _pitch_by_size take the 20th PERCENTILE of those deltas as the block-continuation reference. Fed an interleaved list, that percentile lands in the near-zero population and collapses.
The continuation gate is `0 < gap <= ref * BLOCK_GAP_FACTOR` with BLOCK_GAP_FACTOR = 1.15. With a collapsed ref, every genuine line step is rejected and every line becomes its own block.

measured_on_y06_pdfium.verdict: a genuine 11.50pt line step is REJECTED

group_a.verdict: REJECTED -- one gutter cannot separate three columns

the_mechanism.worked_example: y06 page 20, a MuPDF block of 10 lines at x 80.7..180.7 reading 'Yes. You can claim the / credit for other / dependents for this / dependent. Check the / ...' -- all size 10.0, all left-aligned at 80.7, baselines stepping 9.5-9.9pt. We split it 9 times, every split reported as `gap 9.92 > ref 2.17 x 1.15 = 2.50`.

split_reason_census_y06_first_40_pages._note: Identical ranking on both arms, which is the point.
split_reason_census_y06_first_40_pages._reading: `no horizontal overlap` and `gap exceeds ref` are the SAME root seen twice: interleaved columns put non-overlapping lines next to each other AND collapse the pitch reference. `size change over 6 percent` and `shared baseline too far apart` are separate, smaller causes -- the latter is the documented table-cell limit and is 70% of x10's splits.

blast_radius_lines_per_para._note: Whole corpus, parse+infer only, both arms. `ratio` is reference lines-per-para divided by candidate lines-per-para; 1.00 means the arms agree.

y07_irs_f1040_form._note: The purest instance of the signature: 1.01 lines per block. Tier `unsupported`, so it contributes no pages.

x10_answer._note: Yes -- x10's over-splitting is the same SITE (_build_blocks) but a different failing rule: 70% of its splits are `shared baseline, too far apart`, the documented table-cell limit, not the pitch collapse. Do not expect the pitch fix to close x10.

blast_radius_lines_per_para.gated_corpus: Ten of the sixteen gated documents come out with an identical Para count on both arms because infer._merge_flow_paras repairs the damage downstream. l1_word_native is the exception that does not (4 -> 8 Paras, 3.75 -> 1.88 lines per para), and 05_memo, c5_graphics and 02_research differ slightly. This is why the gate passes today.

proposed_fix_direction._note: Not implemented. Two independent changes; either helps, both is better.

a_n_column_split.what: _column_split returns at most one gutter. Make it return all of them and assemble each band separately, the way _build_blocks already does for two.
a_n_column_split.risk: column detection is geometry-sensitive and every gated document goes through it

b_sanity_floor_the_pitch_reference.what: A body pitch far below the text's own size is not a measurement -- 10pt text cannot step 2.67pt. Reject such a reference and fall back to a size-derived default, the same shape as the right-margin guard in infer.py.
b_sanity_floor_the_pitch_reference.addresses: makes the column-split failure survivable rather than fatal
b_sanity_floor_the_pitch_reference.risk: low and bounded; it only ever RAISES a reference that has collapsed, and a raised reference can only join lines that a correct measurement would have joined
b_sanity_floor_the_pitch_reference.why_preferred_first: it is one site, it is defensive, and it can be gated on measured evidence exactly as MARGIN_MISCLUSTER_PT was

instrument_caveats: The first split-reason census flattened each page's blocks and re-sorted by (y, x) before re-running the assembly, which interleaves columns by construction and made `no horizontal overlap` look like the whole story on both arms. The census recorded here instruments _build_blocks_one in place, so the real _column_split path above it is the one being measured.

The worked example on y06 page 20 quotes reference values computed page-wide by the sampler rather than per column-group. The per-group values that the real code computes are recorded separately under `measured_on_y06_pdfium` and are the authoritative ones; they tell the same story (2.67 page-wide against 11.50 true, on a page where _column_split returned None so page-wide IS the group).
